claims.claim: Do not fill the commit-message body with narration of the obvious diff.
claims.trigger: Writing a commit message during the invoked Git workflow
claims.exceptions: The adjacent sentence directs the body toward motivation, constraints or migration notes; what is obvious requires contextual judgment.
claims.enforcement_effect: Editorial prohibition in the Git procedure, not a mechanical Git restriction.

baseline_comparisons.reason: Registers convention selection and using the body for motivation/constraints/migration, but omits the independently violable prohibition on additional obvious-diff narration.
The line is dismissed as technique; logical commit grouping and PR-description requirements concern different actions.
Although quoting this line, the action and scenario concern logical grouping and Conventional Commits subjects, not redundant body narration.

claims.comparison_reason: The positive body-content direction can be satisfied while adding a separate paragraph narrating obvious changes; neither subject syntax nor logical grouping forbids that additional content.
claims.distinguishing_behavioral_scenario: A Conventional Commit includes a useful motivation paragraph followed by an unnecessary line-by-line restatement of renamed variables. Prior positive body guidance and grouping can hold while this prohibition is violated.
